answer: Each agent registers a secret seed derived from a unique physical sensor reading, like the umber bark pattern of a willow, and hashes it into a commitment posted on the ledger. When a query arrives, a zephyr‑timed reveal phase forces the agent to disclose the original seed; peers verify the hash and reject any duplicate commitments, making pre‑computed Sybil identities useless. An attacker must harvest distinct sensor data and pay the full registration cost for every fabricated node, scaling linearly with the desired Sybil count.
